question: Can one pre-trained single-stream Transformer give a universal image-text representation that transfers to all vision-and-language tasks, and which pre-training tasks matter?
hypothesis: Conditional masking (mask one modality, keep the other intact) and optimal-transport word-region alignment give better joint embeddings than joint random masking and implicit alignment.
contributions: UNITER, a universal image-text representation for V+L tasks
Conditional masking for MLM/MRM and an Optimal-Transport-based Word-Region Alignment pre-training task
New state of the art on a wide range of V+L benchmarks, with ablations on each pre-training task and dataset

method.summary: A single-stream Transformer takes Faster R-CNN region features (plus a 7-d box vector) and WordPiece tokens. It is pre-trained on 5.6M in-domain plus 4M out-of-domain image-text pairs with MLM, MRM (3 variants), ITM and OT-based WRA, one task sampled per mini-batch, then fine-tuned end to end on six V+L tasks.
method.task: multimodal pre-training for vision-and-language tasks (VQA, VCR, NLVR2, SNLI-VE, image-text retrieval, referring expression comprehension)

datasets.name: COCO Captions (pre-training)
datasets.split: raw train+val merged, downstream eval images excluded
datasets.preprocessing: Excluded all val/test images used downstream and Flickr30K images by URL matching (222 images removed in total)

datasets.name: Conceptual Captions
datasets.preprocessing: URL-matching exclusion; 109 images excluded from training (CC+SBU)

datasets.name: VQA
datasets.split: test-dev, test-std; train+val plus Visual Genome QA for test results

datasets.name: COCO retrieval
datasets.split: 82K/5K/5K train/val/test images (Karpathy), plus 30K extra images from COCO val

models.name: UNITER-base
models.architecture: single-stream Transformer over regions and tokens
models.init_from: BERT pre-trained weights (Table 2 L2, MLM text-only on Wikipedia+BookCorpus)

models.name: UNITER-large
models.init_from: inferred: BERT-large weights (the paper only says weights from BERT are used for the base ablation)

models.name: Faster R-CNN
models.init_from: pre-trained on Visual Genome object+attribute data

training.objective: One task sampled per mini-batch: MLM (15% mask: 80% [MASK], 10% random, 10% unchanged), MRM with MRFR (L2), MRC (CE on detector label) and MRC-kl (KL to detector distribution), region mask 15% by zeroing features, ITM (BCE on [CLS], random negative image or text), WRA (OT distance, cosine cost, IPOT with K=1 inner iteration)
training.optimizer: AdamW stated for fine-tuning only; pre-training optimizer not stated
training.hardware: Nvidia V100 16GB PCIe; up to 4 nodes of 4x V100 with Horovod+NCCL over ethernet; fine-tuning on V100 or Titan RTX 24GB
training.compute: 882 V100 GPU hours (base), 3645 V100 GPU hours (large)

other.batching: dynamic sequence length, batches by number of input units (text tokens + image regions); gradient accumulation
other.VCR second-stage pre-training: MLM+MRFR+MRC-kl on VCR, batch 4096 input units, lr 3e-4, weight decay 0.01, max 60K steps
other.fine-tuning VQA: BCE multi-label, batch 10240 units, max 5K steps, AdamW lr 3e-4, wd 0.01
other.fine-tuning VCR: batch 4096 units, max 5K steps, lr 1e-4, wd 0.01; after stage II: lr 6e-5, max 8K steps
other.retrieval hard negatives: two random plus two hard negatives per positive; 128 sampled negatives per text, top 20 kept; refreshed every N=4000 (COCO) or 2500 (Flickr) steps; triplet loss
other.pre-training hyperparameters: not given in this version (batch size, steps, lr, warmup, optimizer)

inference.decoding: VQA: max-probable answer; others classification or ranking
inference.samples: single model per cell; 10-model ensemble only for VCR (Table 9); no seeds reported

limits: Pre-training hyperparameters (optimizer, lr, batch, steps) are not stated, only fine-tuning ones.
Ablations are single runs on UNITER-base with no seeds or significance tests; differences between rows are often under 1 point of Meta-Sum.
Relies on a frozen off-the-shelf Faster R-CNN; the authors list early interaction between raw pixels and tokens as future work.
The detector was trained on COCO images that include RefCOCO val/test images, so RE comprehension numbers are contaminated; the authors ignore this for comparability with concurrent work.
LXMERT pre-trains on downstream VQA-related data, so VQA comparison is not like-for-like.
Text says UNITER-base outperforms others 'across all tasks except VQA', yet Table 3 lists base 72.70/72.91 above LXMERT 72.42/72.54 on VQA; the text and table disagree.
